question: Judith Jarvis Thomson, who named the trolley problem, finally concluded what about the bystander at the switch?
options: He may turn it, but need not
answer: He may not turn it. In 2008 Thomson reversed her verdict. Suppose he could also send the trolley onto himself: if he would not pay that price to save the five, he cannot make the lone worker pay it. So the old puzzle, why he may turn it when a surgeon may not kill, vanished.
move: Before making a stranger pay a price, ask whether you would pay it.
ask: Before I ask someone else to pay a price, would I pay it myself?
trap: Assuming the case's champion kept the verdict almost everyone gives.
reference: Thomson, Turning the Trolley, Philosophy & Public Affairs 36 (4), 2008
